name: Question 16
problem: Let $B={[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}$ and $C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C.$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ relative to the basis $C.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 3 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

On the right-hand side, we obtain the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 16

Let B={[63],[−30]} and C={[12],[03]} be bases of R2. Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C.

a
[2−3−36]
b
[1332]
c
[630−2]
d
[6−3−32]
e
[6331]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's denote the vectors of B and C as {b1,b2} and {c1,c2}, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors of B relative to the basis C.

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of b1 and b2 relative to the basis C. We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix M=[||||c1c2b1b2||||].

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

M=[106−32330]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[106−303−96]R2:=13R2∼[106−301−32]

On the right-hand side, we obtain the change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C. Therefore, we have PB→C=[6−3−32].
